title:
Comment of Fran Durner in Docket(s)/Project(s) P-15423-000
Submission Date: 11/1/2026

documents.name: 152054.txt
documents.text:
Fran Durner, Homer, AK.
As a concept, an underwater data center might sound like a good idea, if it was installed in the right place. 

The Forelands of Cook Inlet is not that place. Cook Inlet, in general, is no place for an underwater data center.

Cook Inlet is an ecologically important body of water for fish, pelagic birds, fishermen and women, as a marine highway, and to the people who live around it. The Forelands is the narrowest part of the Inlet, a bottleneck.

I am opposed to DeepGreen’s proposed Cook Inlet Data Center for the following reasons:

Noise and vibrations generated by the proposed 300 generators would interfere with endangered beluga whales ability to communicate and navigate from Lower to Upper Cook Inlet where they feed and calve.
Many scientific and peer reviewed papers have studied the toxic effect of copper on salmon’s ability to find their way to their spawning streams. The release of copper toxins from the data center infrastructure into the waters of Cook Inlet has the potential to be absolutely disastrous, especially for the people who rely on salmon and salmon fisheries..
Warming of the waters in Cook Inlet from the data center’s waste heat has serious potential impacts on the area’s aquatic ecology and has not been studied.
The data center generators would require constant maintenance because of the silt and mud of the Inlet which is carried there by glacial rivers surrounding the Inlet.
Cook Inlet is not ice free in the winter and experiences some of the most extreme tides in the world. Ice floes, especially at low tide and during winter storms, would pose a constant threat of severe damage to the data center for up to half a year, every year.
The energy demands of the generators during slack tide would strain the local Kenai Peninsula utility company which is already experiencing growing demands.

I cannot think of any reasonable, compelling, or beneficial reason to allow DeepGreen to build an underwater data center in Cook Inlet. 

Please do not let it happen.

Sincerely,
Fran Durner
Homer, Alaska
